newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO market to rise if minister goes over sex probe.
newsitem.headline: OLO market to rise if minister goes over sex probe.

text.p: The Belgian linear bond (OLO) market, unmoved so far by allegations a top government minister broke the law by having sex with young boys, could even rally if he resigned, traders said on Tuesday.
Belgium's parliament on Tuesday set up a committee of inquiry into the allegations against Elio Di Rupo, one of four deputy prime ministers. He vehemently denies the allegations.
OLO dealers said, however, it would be hard for him to undo the damage. If parliament voted to lift his constitutional immunity, "it will be the end for Mr Di Rupo," one said.
Another dealer said the market had fully discounted the possibility that Di Rupo might be forced to resign.

"If he was simply replaced by another francophone socialist the spread (over Bunds) could go back to between 10 and 15 basis points," he said. "We will only see underperformance if the government started to quarrel."

The benchmark 10-year OLO and Belgian franc on Tuesday regained ground lost on Monday in the wake of publication of the allegations on Saturday. The yield ended at 5.96 percent, down from 5.98 at Monday's close. The spread narrowed to 16 from 17 basis points. The franc recovered to 20.6070/90 to the mark.
Money market rates were also steady, with three-month Treasury bills sold at an unchanged average yield of 3.05 percent at the weekly auction.

Dealers said a thin turnout at an exchange auction, where only 11.13 billion francs of OLOs close to maturity were swapped for longer-dated paper, was due to the Treasury's pricing policy. "Conditions were not very good," one trader said.

Dealers agreed most of the volume was probably due to one fund extending the duration of its portfolio. "The price might not have been good, but if they had tried to buy 10 billion in the market it would have been more difficult," one said.
Elsewhere, OLO traders said there was strong buying of the 7.00 percent April 1999 OLO 13.

The market was also talking about a planned issue of certificates of deposit by the Belgian National Bank, although this was not discussed at the Treasury's regular meeting with primary dealers on Monday, one trader said.
After the close, a central bank official confirmed the CD programme, to mop up liquidity resulting from a transfer of gold sales revenues to the Treasury, could start on November 25.
